doc.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019

title: Musical memory, patterns and expectation
summary: They discuss remembering what you just played, and how patterns create expectation.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: So maybe that’s part of your question.
It is. I wonder, how long is your memory —

When you’re improvising. Good one. That was quick. If you’re improvising and you do a particular thing and it worked, then you’re moving on. You know there’s this term like we’re in the moment. But there was a moment a few seconds ago or a few measures ago then you did something, can I safely say that that doesn’t leave your memory? Because you may want to do it again or you may not want to do it again.

Well I aspire toward being in a place where I can actually make that decision, rather than have me just speak on in the other place. When you have the larger picture you realize that it’s happened, then as you said, you see whether it’s relevant. If it has relevance as you move forward or not. But yes, if it’s not too far away I might remember it and use it or not. So I don’t know quite how to get to that or change it. We all, we have patterns you know. We all are — we perceive patterns, amazingly, through a variety of senses, and relate to them. I mean I can speak very specifically about musical patterns and changes and notes and chords and motifs and all that stuff, but just generally human creatures are great at perceiving these patterns and when there’s a pattern, the great choreographer Agnes DeMille said when there’s a pattern there’s an expectation. Every time you have a pattern you’ve created an expectation. So that’s I think to the core of your question, it’s
just being conscious of those expectations and then translating it to my little thing or our little thing about playing jazz you know. As I said it can be any aspect of art or life you know.
